subject.title: In-turn background work (Workflow / run_in_background / Workflow-backed skills) is SIGKILLed at the turn boundary under the claude-cli runtime

question: Should this issue remain the umbrella for claude-cli in-turn background survival plus durable delivery, or should maintainers make the newer source-proven survival issue the canonical owner and keep delivery in the existing queue/ownership issues?
rationale: The source proves the cleanup-to-process-tree-kill path remains, but choosing between denial, bounded drain/detach, and durable delivery changes claude-cli process lifetime, orphan-prevention policy, and user-visible completion semantics.

options.title: Adopt bounded longwork contract
options.body: Detect in-flight CLI-owned background work, bound any cleanup deferral or detachment, snapshot the origin route, and deliver completion or forced-cleanup failure durably.

options.title: Declare unsupported native background work
options.body: Keep turn-end cleanup strict, extend denial or diagnostics to remaining unsupported Claude-native background surfaces, and route users to ACP or OpenClaw exec/process paths.

options.title: Make narrower issues canonical
options.body: Close this only after maintainers explicitly route survival to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/102172 and durable delivery to the existing delivery/queue issues.

recommendation.title: Adopt bounded longwork contract
recommendation.body: Detect in-flight CLI-owned background work, bound any cleanup deferral or detachment, snapshot the origin route, and deliver completion or forced-cleanup failure durably.

likelyOwner.reason: obviyus introduced the Claude live-session process model and is also the author of the current run-lifecycle umbrella, making them the best available owner for the lifecycle direction.
